title: Meet-Week Notice
prompt: The crier taps a notice about realm team meets. Festival lamps are already going up along the quay.

choices.label: Ask about team meets
journal: I asked how teams work. The crier grinned like they'd been waiting.

choices.label: Not my path
journal: I shook my head. The notice stayed. So did the itch.

choices.label: Who wins around here?
journal: They named a few captains. One name stuck like a burr.

title: Blank Team Writ
prompt: Parchment, wax, and a blank team writ wait on the civic desk. Eighty gold, one afternoon, and a name that will be shouted — or forgotten.

choices.label: Register the team
journal: I paid. I named us. The wax took my mark.

choices.label: Need more coin first
journal: I left the writ blank. Next year, maybe.

choices.label: Changed my mind
journal: I walked out lighter — and oddly disappointed.

title: Second Pair of Hands
prompt: A hopeful stranger (or a friend you already trust) waits by the drill lawn. Affinity-matched. Asking if this is a one-soul show.

choices.label: Hire them
journal: We shook on it. The roster felt less lonely.

choices.label: Captain myself
journal: I kept the line short: me, and whoever I become.

choices.label: Not yet
journal: I asked them to check back. Pride and caution argued all evening.

title: First Official Meet
prompt: The arena gate opens for your first official meet. Opposing colors already warm the yard. Ten gold, one act, one chance to look foolish or memorable.

choices.label: Enter the meet
journal: We paid. We stepped in. The board wrote our name in ink that smelled like dust and pride.

choices.label: Skip this year
journal: I kept the coin. The writ stayed quiet another season.

choices.label: Watch from the rail
journal: I studied the bracket without entering. Next year would know their faces.

title: Placement Stands
prompt: The meet ends under festival lamps. Food-stall steam and cheers fill the yard. Your team still smells like effort. The purse is yours — don't trip on the way to the stalls.

choices.label: Accept the purse
journal: Gold landed heavy. So did the noise of our name.

choices.label: Credit the roster
journal: I pointed at them first. The cheer got louder.

choices.label: Stay humble
journal: I nodded once and left before the story got too tall.

title: Familiar Crest
prompt: A captain with a familiar crest blocks the path — not quite a threat, not quite a greeting. New ink on the board, they say. Try to be worth remembering.

choices.label: Offer respect
journal: I tipped my head. Rivalry with manners. Rare, and useful.

choices.label: Mark them a foe
journal: I met their eyes and filed the name under unfinished.

choices.label: Walk past
journal: I kept walking. Some sparks don't need air.

title: Bag Half-Packed
prompt: One of yours waits after drills, bag half-packed. Another hall offered more — or their side still aches. They need to know if this team is a season or a home.

choices.label: Match the offer
journal: Coin left my purse. Loyalty stayed. Barely.

choices.label: Let them go
journal: I opened the gate. The roster felt colder by morning.

choices.label: Ask them to stay for pride
journal: I asked without gold. Pride is a thin rope — sometimes it holds.

title: Circuit Writ
prompt: A circuit writ lists three realm meets before the next big bracket. Your roster looks at the map like a dare. Stay home and you're beloved. Tour and you're remembered farther.

choices.label: Tour the circuit
journal: We took the road. New realms learned our name the hard way — by watching.

choices.label: Stay local
journal: We kept to our home yard. Familiar cheers. Smaller map.

choices.label: Decline the sponsor
journal: I turned down the purse. Independence tasted like dust and freedom.

title: Teams Bracket Banner
prompt: A herald's banner snaps over the arena gate. Every three years the Teams bracket opens beside Blade and Spark. Entry is twenty gold and one hard day. The realm will watch.

choices.label: Enter Teams
journal: We paid. We stepped into the big noise.

choices.label: Skip this cycle
journal: I saved the coin and the nerves for smaller meets.

choices.label: Send the roster without me
journal: They went in my colors. I watched from the shade.

title: Festival Banner Half-Rolled
prompt: A chronicler waits with a blank Codex page and a festival banner half-rolled. Your renown crossed the line the festivals track. The crowd already knows your affinity.

choices.label: Accept the banner
journal: The banner went up. Renown became something you could point at.

choices.label: Stay quiet — ledger only
journal: I took the Codex line and left the cloth rolled. Enough.

choices.label: Sell local name rights
journal: A stall paid to shout us. Coin now. Story a little thinner.

title: Disputed Call
prompt: A disputed ruling hangs over the lawn. The call stands unless you protest in writing. The crowd has opinions. So does your pulse.

choices.label: Protest the call
journal: I filed the writ. Sleep came late and thin.

choices.label: Accept and train harder
journal: I swallowed it. Dawn drills got meaner.

choices.label: Leave the circuit
journal: I packed the banners. Some fights aren't worth the dust.

title: Buyout on the Table
prompt: An offer sits on the table — neat, heavy, and final-looking. They'll take the name, the writ, and the headache. You take the gold and a quieter year.

choices.label: Sell
journal: I sold. The Codex kept the wins. My hands felt empty.

choices.label: Refuse buyout
journal: I left the gold. The headache stayed mine.

choices.label: Disband clean
journal: We ended it ourselves. No rival got the satisfaction.

title: Dusk at the Writ
prompt: Dusk. A familiar face waits where you once waited for your own chance. If you name them, they'll keep the affinity honest. If you don't, they'll still remember the meets.

choices.label: Name them successor
journal: I handed over the writ. The line continued.

choices.label: Dissolve with honors
journal: We ended clean, banners folded, names kept in the Codex.

choices.label: Split credit in the Codex
journal: I wrote us both into the record. Pride shared is still pride.

title: Old Writ, New Eyes
prompt: You wake into a new life. Somewhere a Codex page still lists placements that belonged to someone who shared your stubbornness. Names without a living roster.

choices.label: Read the old wins
journal: I traced the placements. Pride without a roster. Bittersweet and true.

choices.label: Close the Codex
journal: I left the page. New life, new writ someday — or never.

choices.label: Promise a new team
journal: I swore quietly. The echo didn't answer. It didn't need to.

title: Hall Writs Aren't Romance
prompt: Dust and ledgers. A broker eyes you like a possible landlord of trouble. Hall writs mean keys, fees, and people who expect supper after the job.

choices.label: Ask about hall writs
journal: I asked costs and slots. The numbers were honest. Painfully.

choices.label: Not for me
journal: I stepped back. Adventure stayed someone else's headache.

choices.label: Tell me the costs
journal: Gold, age, and a hall slot. I filed it under later.

title: Keys on Wood
prompt: Keys land in your palm. Wood, wax, and the smell of an empty hall. One hundred fifty gold. One hall. Your name on the board. Break the door, you buy the door.

choices.label: Take the hall
journal: I paid. I took the keys. The quiet felt loud.

choices.label: Delay a year
journal: I kept my gold. The empty hall waited for someone else.

choices.label: Walk away
journal: I left the keys on the desk. Freedom weighed less than I'd hoped.

title: Candidate at the Doorframe
prompt: A candidate leans on your doorframe, kit packed, stomach honest. Low fee, they take what jobs they can. Mid, fed and focused. High, their best years — if the board matches.

choices.label: Hire on Low fee
journal: Cheap and risky. We both knew it.

choices.label: Hire on Mid fee
journal: Fair coin. Fair work. A start.

choices.label: Hire on High fee
journal: I paid for excellence. They nodded like it mattered.

choices.label: Pass
journal: I sent them on. The hall stayed quieter.

title: Blank Board, First Client
prompt: Your hall's board is blank. A townsfolk client waits with a small job and a larger question: are you open? Empty pegs. Fresh chalk.

choices.label: Post the board open
journal: Chalk went up. The first ordinary job found us.

choices.label: Stay dark a year
journal: I kept the board bare. Quiet hall. Quiet coin.

choices.label: Post only for known clients
journal: Selective chalk. Safer. Slower.

title: First Real Payout
prompt: The first real payout sits on your hall table. Nobody is dying. That feels like winning. Ordinary thanks from a herb-grower, caravan, or watch post.

choices.label: Collect pay
journal: Gold in the coffer. Proof we exist.

choices.label: Share bonus with roster
journal: I split more than I had to. Faces changed.

choices.label: Ask for their name in the Codex
journal: I wrote the client in. Small names make lasting halls.

title: Fees Eat the Year
prompt: Your senior adventurer doesn't sit. The ledger is open between you. Fees eat the year — raise the board, cut someone, or dip into your own purse. Pick before supper.

choices.label: Raise fees
journal: Higher tier. Higher expectations. Thinner sleep.

choices.label: Cut a member
journal: One kit left the peg. The hall felt wrong-sized.

choices.label: Pay from my purse
journal: My coin, their loyalty. For now.

title: Smiling Map
prompt: Another hall-master smiles with too many teeth and a reasonable map. Nice board, they say. Shame if the good contracts keep finding their door.

choices.label: Undercut
journal: I lowered our take. Jobs came. Pride limped.

choices.label: Specialize our board
journal: We picked a lane and owned it.

choices.label: Propose fair split of districts
journal: We drew lines. Competition got polite. Useful.

title: Wilds Work, Real Teeth
prompt: A frontier client doesn't blink much. The contract ink looks darker than usual. Wilds work. Pay matches the risk — if your people come back.

choices.label: Take the risk
journal: We took it. The year got longer.

choices.label: Refuse
journal: I said no. Sleep was easier. Renown wasn't.

choices.label: Send only the best
journal: The strongest went. The rest kept the hall lights on.

title: Tier Slate
prompt: A broker slides a tier slate across your table. Twenty-five, fifty, seventy-five — that's how the hire pools open. Renown ink is already drying at the next mark. You still only get one door.

choices.label: Expand the roster
journal: More kits on the pegs. More mouths. More reach.

choices.label: Keep the hall small
journal: I held the line. Fewer people. Cleaner nights.

choices.label: Host a flavor banquet (still one hall)
journal: We fed the town like we owned two doors. We still owned one. Worth it.

title: Two Ledgers
prompt: A lucrative job sits beside a thinner, kinder one. It pays. It also leans on people who can't lean back. Your hall's name will follow either choice. Gold isn't the only ledger.

choices.label: Take the gold
journal: We took the fat contract. The quiet afterward had edges.

choices.label: Refuse
journal: I turned it down. The board looked cleaner.

choices.label: Renegotiate terms
journal: I rewrote the job until I could live with it.

title: Civic Options
prompt: The clerk doesn't raise their voice. They don't need to. Someone got hurt on your board's watch. Coin, apology, or a sold hall — those are the civic options.

choices.label: Make restitution
journal: I paid and bowed. The hall kept its door.

choices.label: Deny fault
journal: I argued. The room got colder.

choices.label: Sell the hall
journal: I sold. The Codex kept the contracts. I kept the lesson.

title: Ledger Almost Closed
prompt: The ledger is almost closed. Someone you trust waits for the last line. Keys, roster, and the ugly years — or end clean and give a share to people who need roofs more than renown.

choices.label: Hand over hall
journal: I gave the keys. The board kept breathing.

choices.label: Dissolve
journal: We ended it. Names stayed in the Codex.

choices.label: Endow a charity share
journal: Part of the coffer went to a shrine, primer, widows' purse, or healers. Worth more than a banner.

title: Contract Count Without Keys
prompt: A new life. An old Codex line lists contract counts from a hall that no longer answers to your name. The keys are gone. The contracts aren't.

choices.label: Read the contract count
journal: I read the tally. Quiet pride. No keys needed.

choices.label: Leave it unread
journal: I walked past the page. New doors wait or don't.

choices.label: Swear to open a hall again
journal: I promised another board someday. The echo let me keep that.
